text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - High interest and exchange rates are attracting foreign currency to the Slovak money market.

- Slovakia needs an estimated 1,200 billion crowns worth of investments by the year 2,000 for modernisation projects. Half of this sum could be covered by domestic sources, the rest could covered by foreign credits.

SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - The Czech and Slovak republics will give each other mutual support in their efforts to join western European political, military and economic structures, Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and Czech Parliamentary Chairman Milos Zeman said after meeting on Thursday.
- Meciar is to hold talks with opposition party leaders to discuss possible changes to the election system.
- Slovakia and Uzbekistan signed a treaty on basic relations between the two countries, opening the way for wider political and economic cooperation.
- The government has approved a new concept on basic wages.
PRAVDA - The first destinations of the new Slovak Airline will be Moscow, Zurich, Brussels and St Petersburg.
- Meciar, in his talks with Zeman said relations between the two countries would improve if the question of Slovak gold, which is still in the Czech Republic, were sucessfully solved.
- Druha Obchodna, the owner of Slovak oil and gas storage company Nafta has denied reports that it is negotiating the company's sale to a major western group.
- The average income of individual members of Slovak households grew to 3,454 Slovak crowns a month in 1995, an increase of 55 percent compared to 1991.
SME - The government refused to recommend to parliament the approval of 14 judges, despite the fact that they had been nominated by the Justice Ministry.

- Culture Minister Ivan Hudec said that no proper candidate had been selected by the committee to chose a new drama director for the national theatre, and that he supports the nomination of L. Haverl who was nominated by the theatres's general director.
PRACA - According to a draft law banning smoking in public places, public transportation, railway stations and terminals, fines could range from between 500 to five million crowns.
